Commentary of al-Mawardi (*al-Nukat wa al-Uyun*) on Surah 28, verses 7–9:

﴿And We inspired the mother of Moses﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions:

First: It was an inspiration (*ilham*) from God that He cast into her heart, and it was not prophetic revelation (*wahy nubuwwah*). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah.

Second: It was a dream vision. This is related by Ibn 'Isa.

Third: It was a revelation from God to her through the angels, like His revelation to the prophets. This is related by Qutrub.

﴿To suckle him﴾. Mujahid said: the revelation about nursing came before the birth, and others said it came after the birth.

﴿And if you fear for him﴾, meaning the killing that Pharaoh had ordered against the Children of Israel.

﴿Then cast him into the river﴾. *Al-yamm* means the sea, and it is the Nile.

(p-236) ﴿And do not fear﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: Do not fear that he will drown. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Second: Do not fear that he will be lost. This was said by Yahya ibn Salamah.

﴿Nor grieve﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: Do not grieve over being separated from him. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Second: Do not grieve that he will be killed. Yahya ibn Salam said this.

It is said that she placed him in a chest (*tabut*) five spans long and five spans wide, put the key with the chest, and cast it into the sea after she had nursed him for four months. Others said eight months, according to the account of al-Kalbi.

It is related that when the carpenter finished making the chest, he went to Pharaoh to inform him, and Pharaoh sent with him someone to take it. God then blinded his eye and his heart, so he could not find the way. He became certain that this was the boy whom Pharaoh had feared, and from that time he believed. He was the Believer of the family of Pharaoh.

Ibn 'Abbas said: When she had hidden him from her sight, Satan made her regret it, and she said to herself: "If he had been slaughtered before me, I would have buried him and shrouded him; that would have been dearer to me than casting him with my own hand to the beasts and fish of the sea." Then God said: ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you﴾, and so on to the end of the verse.

Al-Asma'i related: I heard a Bedouin slave-girl reciting:

*"I seek God's forgiveness for all my sins, for I kissed a person unlawfully,*
*Like a gazelle, soft in its graceful coquetry,*
*Until midnight came and I had not prayed it."*

I said: "May God fight you! How eloquent you are!" She said: "Is this considered eloquence, alongside His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We inspired the mother of Moses: suckle him﴾, and so on to the end of the verse? In a single verse He combined two commands, two prohibitions, two reports and two glad tidings."

His saying ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

First: His wife's maidservants picked him up when they went out to fetch water. They found his chest and carried it to her. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: The wife of Pharaoh went out to the river, and she had leprosy. She found his chest and took it, and she was cured of her leprosy. She then said: "This child is blessed." This was said by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

﴿That he might be to them an enemy and a sorrow﴾, meaning that in the end he would become an enemy and a sorrow to them. He was not yet an enemy or a sorrow to them at that moment, because Pharaoh's wife rejoiced in him and loved him intensely. So the outcome is mentioned in place of the present state, as the poet said:

*"Death raises every nursing mother for it, and our homes we build for the ruin of time."*

﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said: "A coolness of the eye for me and for you."﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas that when the men of Pharaoh learned about Moses, they came to slaughter him, but she prevented them, brought him to Pharaoh, and said: "A coolness of the eye for me and for you."

﴿Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son﴾. Pharaoh then said: "A coolness of the eye for you, but as for me, no." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "By the One by Whom an oath is sworn, if Pharaoh had affirmed that he would be a coolness of the eye for him, as his wife affirmed, God would have guided him through it as He guided her. But God denied him that."

Regarding "coolness of the eye" there are two interpretations:

First: It cooled her with joy, derived from *qarr*, which means coolness.

Second: Her tears remained in her eye and did not flow out because of sorrow. This is derived from *qarra fi al-makan*, meaning he settled in the place when he stayed there.

﴿While they did not perceive﴾, that their destruction would be at his hands and in his time.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verse 20:

His saying: ﴿And there came a man running from the farthest part of the city﴾. Al-Dahhak said: He was the believer of the family of Pharaoh.

Shu'ayb said: His name was Sham'un.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Sham'an.

Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: His name was Hizqil ibn Sham'un.

Al-Kalbi said: He was the son of Pharaoh's paternal uncle, the brother of his father.

﴿He said: O Musa, the chiefs are conferring about you to kill you﴾. In this there are two interpretations:

The first: They are consulting about killing you. This was said by al-Kalbi, and from it is the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab:

"I see the people have invented a custom, and in every new matter there is consultation (yu'tamar)."

The second: Some of them command others to kill you. From it is His saying: ﴿And consult among yourselves with kindness﴾ [al-Talaq: 6], meaning that some of you command others. Likewise is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"O Ahar ibn 'Amr, as if I were intoxicated, and what the man commands (ya'tamir) overtakes him."

(p-245)

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verse 43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, has two interpretations:

The first: it refers to the seven oft-repeated verses (al-mathani), which Allah sent down upon His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, and he related it as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report.

The second: it refers to the Torah. This was said by Qatadah.

Yahya ibn Salam said: it is the first Book in which the obligatory duties (al-faraʾid), the prescribed punishments (al-hudud), and the rulings (al-ahkam) were sent down.

﴿After We had destroyed the former generations﴾. Abu Saʿid al-Khudri said: Allah did not destroy any nation of the nations, nor any generation of the generations, nor any town of the towns, with a punishment from the sky or from the earth, since Allah sent down the Torah upon the face of the earth, except the town whose people Allah transformed into monkeys. Have you not seen His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book after We had destroyed the former generations﴾?

(p-255) The meaning of His saying: ﴿as insights for mankind﴾ is: clear evidences.

﴿And guidance﴾ means: a direction (dalalah), ﴿and mercy﴾ means: a blessing (niʿmah).

﴿That they may remember﴾ means: that they may recall this blessing, so that they remain steadfast in their faith in this world and be assured of their reward in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verse 44–47:

His saying: ﴿And you were not at the side of the mount when We called﴾. This is an address to the Prophet ﷺ: "And you were not, O Muhammad, at the side of the mount when We called." In this there are two interpretations:

One of them: it was called, "O community of Muhammad, I have answered you before you called upon Me, and I have given you before you asked Me." This was said by Abu Hurayrah.

The second: they were called in the loins of their fathers, that they should believe in you when you are sent. This was said by Muqatil.

﴿But it was a mercy from your Lord﴾. In this there are two interpretations:

One of them: that what Moses was called with from the side of the mount is a remembrance of you, a blessing from your Lord.

The second: that your being sent as a prophet to your people is a blessing from your Lord.

﴿That you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾. He means the Arabs. (p-256)

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verses 48–51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: "Two kinds of sorcery, supporting each other."﴾ The Kufans read sihrani (two sorceries). As for those who read saahirani (two sorcerers), there are three opinions:

The first: Musa and Muhammad, peace be upon them both. This is the saying of the polytheist Arabs, and Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan said it.

The second: Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both. This is the saying of the Jews regarding them both at the beginning of the mission. Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and Abu Zayd said it.

The third: 'Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ). This is the saying of the Jews today, and Qatada said it.

As for those who read sihrani (two sorceries), there are three opinions:

The first: they are the Torah and the Qur'an. 'Asim al-Jahdari and al-Suddi said it.

The second: the Torah and the Injil (Gospel). Isma'il and Abu Mijlaz said it.

The third: the Injil and the Qur'an. Qatada said it.

﴿And they said: "Indeed, we are disbelievers in each of them."﴾ That is, in what was mentioned, according to the differing opinions. Regarding the speakers of this, there are two sayings. One: the Jews. The second: the Quraysh.

His saying: ﴿And We have certainly caused the Word to reach them﴾ has three meanings:

The first: its meaning is "We made the Word clear to them." This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: "We completed one thing with another, as your connecting [of words]." This was said by al-Akhfash.

The third: "We made one part follow another." This was said by 'Ali ibn 'Isa.

Regarding ﴿the Word﴾ there are two views:

One of them: that the report is about this world and the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: informing them of whom We destroyed from the people of Nuh with such-and-such, the people of Salih with such-and-such, and the people of Hud with such-and-such.

﴿So that they may remember﴾ has three meanings:

The first: they remember Muhammad and so believe in him. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: they remember and so fear that what befell those before them will befall them. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

The third: "So that they may take heed through the Qur'an from the worship of idols." This was related by al-Naqqash.

The second: Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both. This is the saying of the Jews regarding them both at the beginning of the mission. Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and Abu Zayd said it.

The third: 'Isa and Muhammad (ﷺ). This is the saying of the Jews today, and Qatada said it.

The first: they are the Torah and the Qur'an. 'Asim al-Jahdari and al-Suddi said it.

The second: the Torah and the Injil (Gospel). Isma'il and Abu Mijlaz said it.

The second: "We completed one thing with another, as your connecting [of words]." This was said by al-Akhfash.

The third: "We made one part follow another." This was said by 'Ali ibn 'Isa.

One of them: that the report is about this world and the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: informing them of whom We destroyed from the people of Nuh with such-and-such, the people of Salih with such-and-such, and the people of Hud with such-and-such.

The first: they remember Muhammad and so believe in him. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Second: Those to whom We gave the Torah and the Gospel before Muhammad believe in Muhammad. This was said by Ibn Shajara.

First: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam, Tamim al-Dari, al-Jarud al-Abdi and Salman al-Farisi, who embraced Islam, and this verse and the one after it were revealed concerning them. This was said by Qatada.

Third: They repel with greeting the ugliness of encounter. This is the meaning of the saying of al-Naqqash.

Fifth: They repel with good the evil. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

It may also permit a sixth: they repel by repentance what preceded of disobedience.

First: They give zakat voluntarily. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

Second: A man's spending on his family, and this was before the revelation of zakat. This was said by al-Suddi.

Third: They give charity from their earnings. This was said by Qatada.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾. Concerning this there are four sayings:

First: They are a people from the Jews who embraced Islam, and the Jews would confront them with insults and abuse, so they turned away from them. This was said by Mujahid.

Second: They are a people from the Jews who embraced Islam, and whenever they heard what the Jews had altered and changed in the Torah from the description and attributes of Muhammad ﷺ, they turned away from it and disliked its alteration. This was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

Second: To us our forbearance and to you your folly.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ has two interpretations:

First: whom you love to be guided.

Second: whom you love because of kinship. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Hasan: it was revealed concerning Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his uncle Abu Talib: "Say, 'There is no god but Allah'; I will testify for you by it before Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection." He said: "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me for it, I would have gladdened your eyes by it." Mujahid narrated that he said: "O son of my brother, the religion of the elders," and so the verse was revealed, referring to Abu Talib.

﴿But Allah guides whom He wills﴾. Qatadah said: this refers to al-ʿAbbas.

﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾. Mujahid said: this means those for whom guidance and misguidance have been decreed.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "If we follow the guidance with you, we would be swept from our land."﴾ It was said that this verse was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn ʿUthman ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manaf al-Qurashi, who said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We know that what you say is true, but what prevents us from following the guidance with you and believing in you is our fear that the Arabs will snatch us from our land," meaning Mecca, "for we are the morsel of the Arabs' head, and we have no strength against them." So Allah answered what he had raised as an objection, saying: ﴿Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

First: He made it secure by the nature He placed in souls, of inclination toward it, so that the gazelle, the wolf, the dove and the kite do not flee from it.

Second: He made it secure by the command issued from Him, granting safety to whoever enters it and takes refuge in it. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The meaning is: "You were secure in My sanctuary, eating My provision while worshipping other than Me. Will you then fear when you worship Me and believe in Me?"

﴿To which are brought the fruits of every thing﴾, that is, the fruits of every land and region are gathered to it.

First: they do not reason, said by al-Dahhak.

Second: they do not reflect, said by Ibn Shajarah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verses 68–70:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses﴾ have three interpretations:

The first: Some people used to set aside the best of their wealth for their families in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). So He said: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills﴾ from His creation, ﴿and chooses﴾ whomever He wills for His obedience. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills﴾ of creation, ﴿and chooses﴾ whomever He wills for His prophethood. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The third: ﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills﴾ – the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) – ﴿and chooses﴾ the Ansar for His religion. This was related by al-Naqqash.

(p-263) ﴿They have no choice﴾ (ma kana lahumu al-khiyarah). Regarding this, there are two possibilities:

The first: its meaning is, "And He chooses for the believers what good (khayr) they have in it," so this is an affirmation (ithbat).

The second: its meaning is, "It is not for creatures to have a choice over Allah," so this is a negation (nafy).

Those who held this view have two opinions regarding the intended referent:

The first: He meant by this a group of polytheists who assigned to Allah a portion of the produce and livestock that He had created, saying, "This is for Allah, by their claim, and this is for our partners." So this was revealed concerning them. This was said by Ibn Shajarah.

The second: It was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah when he said what Allah related about him in Surat al-Zukhruf: ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man..."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31], meaning himself and 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. So Allah said: ﴿They have no choice﴾ – that they should choose over Allah the prophets.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verse 76–77:

The Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾. Ibn Abbas said: He was the son of his paternal uncle. Qatadah said: Qarun was the son of the paternal uncle of Musa, the brother of his father. He had crossed the sea with the Children of Israel, and he was called al-Munawwar (the Illuminated), because of the beauty of his voice in reciting the Torah. But the enemy of Allah became a hypocrite, just as al-Samiri became a hypocrite.

﴿So he oppressed them﴾. Concerning this there are six opinions:

The first: his oppression of them was that he disbelieved in Allah. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: that he lengthened the hems of his garments by a span. This was said by Shahr ibn Hawshab.

The third: that he exalted himself over them through the abundance of his wealth and children. This was said by Qatadah.

The fourth: that he committed an act of lewdness (baghy) when Allah commanded Musa to stone the adulterer. Qarun deliberately approached a prostitute, gave her wealth, and induced her to claim against him that he had committed adultery with her, and he said: "You have committed adultery."

The prostitute came forward and made that claim against him. What she said weighed heavily on Musa, and he made her swear by Allah, who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Musa, that she tell the truth. She said: "I bear witness that you are innocent, and that Qarun gave me wealth and induced me to say what I said. You are the truthful one, and Qarun is the liar." This was his oppression, said Ibn Abbas. Al-Suddi said: The name of the prostitute was Shajarata, and Qarun offered her two thousand dirhams.

The fifth: that he was a slave of Pharaoh who transgressed against the Children of Israel and wronged them. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The sixth: that he attributed what Allah had given him of treasures to himself, by his knowledge and his cunning. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

﴿And We gave him of the treasures﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: that he came upon a treasure from the treasures of Yusuf, peace be upon him. This was said by Ata.

The second: that he practised alchemy (al-kimya’, i.e., the transmutation of metals). This was said by al-Walid.

﴿Indeed, its keys﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions:

The first: its treasuries. This was said by al-Suddi and Abu Razin.

The second: its containers. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The third: the keys of its treasuries, which were made of leather and which forty mules would carry.

The fourth: that the keys of the treasures are the comprehensiveness of his knowledge of them. Ibn Bahr related this, citing the saying of Allah: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ [al-An‘am: 59].

﴿Would weigh down with the group﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: they would weigh down the group. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Abu Salih and al-Suddi.

The second: they would make the group lean over. This was said by al-Rabi‘ ibn Anas. It is derived from al-na’y, which means distance. The poet said:

They keep away from us, yet their affection does not distance itself, and the heart remains held captive among them wherever they are.

The third: the group would stagger under them, as the poet said:

We found a successor, a wretched successor, a slave who, when he staggers under the burden, collapses.

The ‘usbah (group) is the company of people who support one another. Its number has been disputed, with seven opinions:

The first: seventy men. This was said by Abu Salih.

The second: forty men. This was said by al-Hakam, Qatadah and al-Dahhak.

The third: between ten and forty. This was said by al-Suddi.

The fourth: between ten and fifteen. This was said by Mujahid.

The fifth: six or seven. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

The sixth: between three and nine, and they are the nafar (party). This was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

The seventh: ten, based on the saying of the brothers of Yusuf: ﴿And we are a group﴾ [Yusuf: 8]. This was said by al-Kalbi and Muqatil.

Abu Ubaydah claimed that this is of the inverted construction (al-maqlub), its interpretation being: "Indeed the group would weigh down with the keys."

﴿Possessors of strength﴾. Al-Suddi said: possessors of might.

﴿When his people said to him﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: that it was the saying of the believers among them. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: that it was the saying of Musa. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

﴿Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: do not transgress; indeed Allah does not love the transgressors. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: do not be stingy; indeed Allah does not love the stingy. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

The third: do not be insolent; indeed Allah does not love the insolent. This was said by al-Suddi, and the poet said:

I am not one who exults when fortune pleases me, nor one who despairs of its overpowering reversal.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Final Abode﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: seeking lawful provision in one's earnings. This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: that it is charity and the maintenance of kinship ties. This was said by al-Suddi.

It may also bear a third meaning, which is more general: that one draws near to Allah through the blessings He has bestowed. By "the Final Abode" is meant Paradise.

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: do not forget your portion of this world, which is to work in it for your Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: do not forget your self-sufficiency through what Allah has made lawful for you, in preference to what He has forbidden you. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: do not forget to thank Allah for His blessings upon you by obedience. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Zayd.

The second [sense]: and do well in what Allah has made obligatory upon you, as He has done well to you in His bounty. This is the meaning of the saying of Yahya ibn Sallam.

The third: do well in seeking the lawful, as He has done well to you in making it lawful.

﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾. It may bear two meanings:

The first: do not act in it through sins.

The second: do not sever [ties].

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

The first: He does not love the deeds of the corrupters. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: He does not bring the corrupters near. This was said by Ibn Qutaybah.

The seventh: ten, based on the saying of the brothers of Yusuf: ﴿And we are a group﴾ [Yusuf: 8]. This was said by al-Kalbi and Muqatil.

Abu Ubaydah claimed that this is of the inverted construction (al-maqlub), its interpretation being: "Indeed the group would weigh down with the keys."

﴿Possessors of strength﴾. Al-Suddi said: possessors of might.

﴿When his people said to him﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

One: that it was the saying of the believers among them. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: that it was the saying of Musa. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

﴿Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: do not transgress; indeed Allah does not love the transgressors. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: do not be stingy; indeed Allah does not love the stingy. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

The third: do not be insolent; indeed Allah does not love the insolent. This was said by al-Suddi, and the poet said:

I am not one who exults when fortune pleases me, nor one who despairs of its overpowering reversal.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Final Abode﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: seeking lawful provision in one's earnings. This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: that it is charity and the maintenance of kinship ties. This was said by al-Suddi.

It may also bear a third meaning, which is more general: that one draws near to Allah through the blessings He has bestowed. By "the Final Abode" is meant Paradise.

﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: do not forget your portion of this world, which is to work in it for your Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: do not forget your self-sufficiency through what Allah has made lawful for you, in preference to what He has forbidden you. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: do not forget to thank Allah for His blessings upon you by obedience. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Zayd.

The second [sense]: and do well in what Allah has made obligatory upon you, as He has done well to you in His bounty. This is the meaning of the saying of Yahya ibn Sallam.

The third: do well in seeking the lawful, as He has done well to you in making it lawful.

﴿And do not seek corruption in the earth﴾. It may bear two meanings:

The first: do not act in it through sins.

The second: do not sever [ties].

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

The first: He does not love the deeds of the corrupters. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: He does not bring the corrupters near. This was said by Ibn Qutaybah.

He said, ﴿I have been given it only on knowledge that is with me﴾. In this there are five interpretations:

First: that is, by my own strength and knowledge. This was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

Second: on goodness and knowledge that is with me. This was said by Qatadah.

Third: for God's pleasure with me and His knowledge of my deserving it. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Fourth: on knowledge of the ways of acquiring wealth. This was said by Ibn Isa.

Fifth: the knowledge of the craft of *kimiya* (alchemy).

al-Naqqash related that Musa (ʿalayhi al-salam) taught Qarun one third of the craft of *kimiya* (alchemy), taught Yusha ibn Nun one third, and taught the two sons of Harun one third. Qarun deceived them both, and he remained upon his faith until he learned what they had, and he practiced alchemy, and his wealth increased.

Regarding His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾, there are four interpretations:

First: they will be punished and will not be called to account. This was said by Qatadah.

Second: they will not be asked to count them, and they will be given their records, so they will recognize them and acknowledge them. This was said by al-Rabiʿ.

(p-٢٦٩)Third: because the angels will recognize them by their marks, so do not ask about them. This was said by Mujahid.

Fourth: that they will not be asked in the manner of seeking amends, "Why did you not believe?" This was said by Ibn Bahr, as He said, ﴿nor will they be given the chance to make amends﴾ [al-Rum: 57].

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verse 79–80:

His saying: ﴿So he went out before his people in his adornment.﴾ On this there are three opinions:

First: "In his retinue (hashm)." This is the view of Qatada.

Second: "In his followers, seventy thousand, wearing al-mu'asfarat (garments dyed with safflower/saffron-yellow)." This was the first day on which al-mu'asfarat were seen. This is the view of Ibn Zayd. Abu Lababa said: "The first to dye with black was Qarun."

Third: "He went out with white litters (jiwar, sing. jariya) upon white mules, with saddles of gold, on cushions of crimson (uruwan)." This is the view of al-Suddi.

﴿Those who desired the life of this world said: "Oh, would that we had the like of what Qarun was given!"﴾ They wished for his wealth, out of desire for the world.

﴿Indeed, he is one of great fortune.﴾ On this there are two opinions:

First: "He is one of great rank." This is the view of al-Dahhak.

Second: "He is one of great good fortune (jidd)." This is the view of al-Suddi.

(p-270) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: When Musa complained to God about the matter of Qarun, God commanded the earth to obey Musa. When Qarun and his followers approached, Musa said, "O earth, seize them," and it seized them up to their ankles. Then he said, "Seize them," and it seized them up to their waists. Then he said, "Seize them," and it seized them up to their necks. Then he said, "Seize them," and God caused them to be swallowed up, along with Qarun's home and his treasures.

Yazid al-Raqashi narrated that when the earth had seized Qarun up to his neck, Musa took his sandals and struck his face with them. Qarun said, "O Musa, have mercy on me!" God, exalted is He, said: "O Musa, how hard is your heart! My servant called upon you and asked you for mercy, and you did not show him mercy. By My might, if My servant had called upon Me, I would have answered him."

Samurah ibn Jundab narrated that Qarun and his people are made to sink each day by the measure of a man's height, and they will not reach the lowest earth until the Day of Resurrection.

Muqatil said: When Musa commanded the earth and it swallowed him, the Children of Israel said, "He only destroyed him so that he could inherit his wealth, for he was the son of his paternal uncle's brother." So God caused the earth to swallow his home and all his wealth after three days.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who had wished to be in his place the day before began to say, "Woe! It is as if God...﴾ On this there are eight interpretations:

The first: its meaning is, "Do they not know that God...?" Narrated by Mamar from Qatadah.

The second: "Do they not see?" Narrated by Said from Qatadah.

The third: "But God" in the dialect of Himyar, said by al-Dahhak.

The fourth: "And indeed God," with the yāʾ and the kāf being additional connecting particles, related by al-Naqqash.

The fifth: "As if God," with the yāʾ alone being an additional connecting particle.

Ibn ʿIsa said the same interpretation, except that he made the yāʾ serve for alerting (tanbīh).

The sixth: its meaning is "Woe, that God..." Here the particle ويك is separated, with the kāf and the alif divided, and ويك is taken to mean ويح (woe), with the ḥāʾ replaced by a kāf. From this is the verse of ʿAntarah:

"And indeed he has healed my soul and cured its sickness, the saying of the horsemen: 'Woe, ʿAntar, advance!'"

The seventh: "Woe to you, indeed God..." where the lām is omitted for brevity; related by Ibn Shajarah.

The eighth: ويْ is separate, an expression of wonder, and then he resumed, saying "kaʾanna Allah," said by al-Khalil.

The third: He constricts, and this is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Zayd.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We shall assign it to those who do not seek exaltation on the earth﴾, meaning: "We shall make it (Paradise)."

﴿Exaltation (ʿuluwwan)﴾ has six aspects:

First: it means oppression (baghy). This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

Second: arrogance (takabbur). This was said by Muslim.

Third: nobility and honor (sharaf wa ʿizz). This was said by al-Hasan.

Fourth: injustice (ẓulm). This was said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

Fifth: polytheism (shirk). This was said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām.

Sixth: they do not grieve over its humiliation nor compete for its honor. This was said by Abū Muʿāwiya.

It may also admit a seventh: that it means having authority over people therein.

﴿Nor corruption (fasād)﴾ has three interpretations:

First: it is seizing (property or people) by unjust means. This was said by Muslim.

Second: it is acting in acts of disobedience. This was said by ʿIkrima.

Third: it is killing the prophets and the believers. This was said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām.

It may also admit a fourth: bad conduct.

﴿And the good end is for the God-conscious (al-muttaqīn)﴾ has two aspects:

One: the reward is for the God-conscious. This was said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 28, verses 85–88:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you﴾ has five interpretations:

First: He sent down the Qur'an upon you. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam and al-Farra'.

Second: He gave it to you. This was said by Mujahid.

Third: He made it obligatory upon you to act by it. This was related by al-Naqqash.

Fourth: He entrusted you with conveying it and charged you with delivering it. This was related by Ibn Shajara.

Fifth: He explained it upon your tongue. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

It may also bear a sixth meaning: that He decreed for you the sending down of it at its appointed times, because al-Fard (ordaining) means al-taqdir (decreeing).

﴿Will surely bring you back to a place of return﴾ has five aspects:

First: To Makkah. This was said by Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Ibn Jubayr, and al-Suddi.

Second: To Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). This was said by Nu'aym al-Qari'.

Third: To death. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah.

Fourth: To the Day of Resurrection. This was said by al-Hasan.

Fifth: To Paradise. This was said by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.

It is also said that this verse was revealed at al-Juhfa, when the road was difficult for him on the way there; so it is neither Makkan nor Madinan.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ has six interpretations:

(p-273) First: Its meaning is "except He." This was said by al-Dahhak.

Second: Except that which is intended by His Face. This was said by Sufyan al-Thawri.

Third: Except His dominion. This was related by Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari.

Fourth: Except the scholars, for their knowledge remains. This was said by Mujahid.

Fifth: Except His standing (jah), as one says of so-and-so that he has a "face" among the people, meaning standing. This was said by Abu 'Ubayda.

Sixth: The Face means the deed, and from it is the saying: whoever prays at night, his face becomes beautiful by day, meaning his deed.

The poet said:

"I seek forgiveness from God for a sin I cannot count,
Lord of the servants; to Him is the face and the deed."

﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾ has two aspects:

One: The judgment over His creation with what He wills of His command. This was said by al-Dahhak and Ibn Shajara.

Second: That His servants have no right to judge except by His command. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, where He rewards the good-doer and punishes the wrongdoer. And God knows best.
